core_problem_solved: To provide a simple and standardized framework for writing and running repeatable, automated tests for Java code, serving as the foundation for Test-Driven Development (TDD).
key_features: An annotation-based model for defining tests (`@Test`) and lifecycle methods (`@Before`, `@After`)
A test runner for executing tests and collecting results
A set of assertion methods (`Assert.assertEquals`, etc.) for verifying outcomes
era_and_niche: The de facto standard unit testing framework for Java for over a decade. JUnit 4, represented by this coordinate, revolutionized Java testing by introducing annotations, replacing the older inheritance-based model of JUnit 3.
reason_for_obsolescence: This artifact represents JUnit 4, which is now a **legacy framework**. It has been officially superseded by the completely redesigned **JUnit 5 (Jupiter)**. The modern coordinates are `org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter-api` (for writing tests) and `org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter-engine` (for running them). All new projects should use JUnit 5 for its modularity and powerful new features.
